I'm listing the constraints for the feed: no dependencies, skipping unpublished posts because of the embargo, absolute URLs, and keeping permalinks stable. The dev server injects a script into every file, XML included, which would break the feed just as it already does the sitemap. I still need to settle between Atom and RSS 2.0, and the dates have to follow RFC 822.

I'm settling the remaining details: the date format, escaping, and item ordering, with newest posts first and a cap of 20 items. The GUID will be the absolute permalink, and I'll set lastBuildDate from the latest post rather than the current time so the output stays reproducible.

payload.text:
I've read the whole repo, and I made no changes. Here's the plan.

## What the repo looks like now
- `build(site, posts, now)` in `src/build.js` returns a map of output paths to file contents. It already writes `/sitemap.xml` through `src/sitemap.js`.
- `site.json` already has `title`, `baseUrl` and `author`, which is everything an RSS channel needs.
- **Rules the feed must follow:**
  - **No dependencies.** Sites copy this folder into their own repo, so only Node built-ins are allowed and `package.json` dependencies stay empty (`docs/CONTRIBUTING.md`). The XML gets built by hand, the same way the sitemap is.
  - **Only published posts.** Drafts and future-dated posts must stay out. The repo has a post dated 2027-01-15 that's "under embargo until launch". Every post has to pass `isPublished(p, now)`. The sitemap had to be fixed for exactly this in commit 91ce99b.
  - **Links must keep the base path.** Sites are often served under a path like `https://example.test/blog`, so every link has to go through `absoluteUrl(site, permalink(p))`. Permalinks never change.

## Plan
1. **New `src/feed.js`** exporting `feed(site, posts, now = Date.now())`, built like `sitemap.js`:
   - It keeps only posts where `isPublished(p, now)` is true, puts the newest first (`loadPosts` returns oldest first, sorted by filename) and keeps the 20 most recent.
   - It writes RSS 2.0. The channel gets `title`, `link` (the site's home page, via `absoluteUrl(site, '/')`), `description`, and an `atom:link rel="self"` pointing to the feed's own URL.
   - Each item gets `title`, `link`, a `guid isPermaLink="true"` set to the same absolute permalink, `pubDate` and `description`. Using the permalink as the guid stops feed readers from showing old posts as new.
   - Dates use `new Date(p.publish_at).toUTCString()`, the date format RSS expects.
   - `lastBuildDate` is set to the newest post's date, not the current time, so building twice gives the same file.
2. **Escaping.** Titles and bodies go through the existing `escapeHtml`, which already handles `& < > "`. Note that `p.body` is raw text right now (there's no markdown step yet), so the item description is just the escaped body.
3. **Wire it into the build.** Add `out['/feed.xml'] = feed(site, posts, now);` in `build.js`.
4. **Let browsers and readers find it.** Add `<link rel="alternate" type="application/rss+xml" href="…/feed.xml">` to the page HTML. Pages are bare `<h1>` + body right now, so this goes wherever the page `<head>` ends up, or into the theme. The href is built with `absoluteUrl`.
5. **Fix the dev server.** `devserver.js` appends a live-reload `<script>` to every response, so XML files come out broken in dev. The sitemap already has this problem. The fix is to inject the script only into `.html` responses and send the right content type (`application/rss+xml` / `application/xml`).
6. **Tests: new `test/feed.test.js`** using the existing posts and `now = 2026-11-01`:
   - Only `hello-world` appears. The draft and the 2027 embargoed post must not.
   - Links keep the `/blog` base path: `https://example.test/blog/2026/10/hello-world/`.
   - Titles with `&` or `<` come out escaped.
   - Items are newest first and capped at 20.
   - The output is the same on repeated builds.
7. **Docs.** Add a README line saying the feed is at `/feed.xml`.

## Questions for you
- **RSS 2.0 or Atom?** I'd go with RSS since that's what readers asked for, and Atom would be a small change later.
- **Full post or excerpt in each item?** I'd put the full body in for now.
- **Description field:** should we add an optional `description` to `site.json`, or reuse `title`?

The whole change is about 40 lines plus tests and only touches `build.js` and `devserver.js` outside the new file.
